title: How to use gift cards to stack sats

body_text: Most people think of gift cards as a last-minute present or a way to give someone a choice. But inside the Fold app, gift cards are one of the most effective tools for earning bitcoin on purchases you were already going to make. The concept is simple: buy a gift card for a store you already shop at, earn bitcoin back at the moment of purchase, then use the card like normal. Here's a step-by-step breakdown of how it works, with examples and a few tips for getting the most out of every purchase. How it works, step by step Open the Fold app and tap the Shop tab. Browse by category or search for a specific brand. Select the brand and choose the amount you want to load onto the card. Complete the purchase. Your bitcoin reward is credited to your account automatically. Use the gift card at checkout as you normally would. The card delivers digitally, usually within seconds. That's the whole process. The bitcoin goes into your Fold balance. The gift card goes in your wallet or saved to your phone. There are no extra steps at checkout and nothing to redeem later. What this looks like in real life Here are a few ways Fold customers use the gift card marketplace to stack sats on everyday spending: Groceries: Buy an Instacart, Kroger, or grocery chain gift card before you shop. Earn bitcoin on the full amount, then use the card on your weekly grocery order. Travel: Book a trip with a Southwest, Delta, or Airbnb gift card. The bitcoin reward comes through on the gift card purchase, and you use the card to pay for your booking as usual. Dining: Pick up a Chipotle, DoorDash, or Cheesecake Factory card before your next meal out or delivery order. Earn bitcoin on the full card amount. Home improvement: A Home Depot or Lowe's card before your next project means every dollar of materials earns bitcoin automatically. Back to school: Staples, Office Depot, Best Buy, and clothing retailers are all in the marketplace. Load up before the school shopping run and earn bitcoin on the full haul. Tips for getting the most out of the gift card marketplace Check the boosted tab first. Fold runs boosted promotions regularly on specific gift card categories. During a boost window, the bitcoin back rate goes higher than usual. Checking the boosted tab before you buy takes about 10 seconds and can make a meaningful difference in what you earn. Buy before you shop, not after. The bitcoin reward is earned at the moment you buy the gift card, not when you spend it. That means you earn on the full amount you load, regardless of what you end up buying. Get in the habit of picking up the gift card first, then heading to the store or shopping online. Favorite the brands you buy most. The Shop tab lets you save brands to a favorites list so they're always one tap away. If you buy the same few brands every week, favoriting them saves you time on every trip. Load what you plan to spend. You earn bitcoin on the full amount you load onto the card. If you know you'll spend around $100 at a store this week, load that amount and earn bitcoin on the whole thing upfront. Frequently asked questions Can I use gift cards the same way I'd normally use them? Yes. Gift cards bought through Fold work exactly like gift cards purchased anywhere else. You get a digital code, barcode, or link you can use at checkout, in-store or online. When does the bitcoin show up in my account? The bitcoin reward is credited automatically at the time of purchase. You don't need to wait until you spend the gift card or take any additional action. How many brands are in the marketplace? Hundreds. The marketplace spans groceries, dining, travel, retail, home improvement, electronics, entertainment, and more. You can browse by category or search for a specific brand in the app. Ready to try it? Open the Fold app and explore the gift card marketplace. Find the brands you already shop at, check the boosted tab for higher-earning options, and start turning everyday purchases into automatic bitcoin rewards.

title: 4 Things to Know About Ford’s Second-Quarter Results
summary: CFO Sherry House recaps Ford's Q2 2026 earnings, covering profitability, margins, cash flow, and Ford+ momentum.
body_text: Earlier today, we published Ford’s second-quarter 2026 financial results. As I reflect on our performance, what stands out to me most is the momentum and discipline across our global team. The big picture story this quarter is simple: Our Ford+ plan is delivering, our industrial execution continues to strengthen, and our core underlying business is more resilient. For the quarter, Ford generated $48.3 billion in revenue and $2.5 billion in adjusted EBIT — a 17% increase year-over-year. We also generated $2.1 billion in adjusted free cash flow, bringing our total liquidity to over $43 billion. Because of this operating strength, we raised our full-year adjusted EBIT outlook by $1 billion at the midpoint, now expecting between $10 billion and $11 billion for 2026. If you’re following the news today, here are the four key takeaways you need to know about our progress and where we’re headed next: 1. We delivered strong results — and our net loss reflects a planned future investment. Because of our strong operational results in the first half of the year, we increased our full-year profit outlook by $1 billion. You will also see headlines noting that we reported a GAAP net loss of $1.3 billion for Q2. It’s important to understand the context behind that number: most of it was driven by a scheduled, one-time $3.6 billion special item charge resulting from the disposition of our BlueOval SK (BOSK) joint venture in May and charges tied to the EV program cancellations we announced in December 2025.. This was a deliberate step. Crucially, over $3 billion of this charge is non-cash. By restructuring this joint venture, we cleared the runway to repurpose those manufacturing assets for Ford Energy — our high-growth battery energy storage business. This charge was fully expected, previously disclosed, and does not reflect the day-to-day health of our core business, which is healthy, growing, and fundamentally improving. 2. Quality and cost discipline are transforming our core automotive business. A stronger automotive core begins with getting the fundamentals right: quality, cost, and capitalizing on the iconic vehicles our customers love. No. 1 in Quality: Ford was ranked the No. 1 mainstream brand in the J.D. Power 2026 Initial Quality Study — a historic milestone that reflects our company-wide obsession with getting quality right at launch. This progress is central to our drive to take $1 billion in warranty and material costs out of our business this year. Ford Blue: Delivered $1.1 billion in EBIT — up 72% year-over-year — powered by strong pricing and product mix. F-Series expanded its lead as America’s top-selling truck, the Bronco family achieved record Q2 sales, and Maverick Hybrid set a record as the best-selling hybrid pickup in the U.S. Ford Pro: Generated $1.7 billion in profit, demonstrating the resilience of our commercial business despite temporary aluminum supply chain disruptions. Customer demand remains high, with 2027 model year contracting running a full month ahead of last year’s pace. Model e: Marked its third consecutive quarter of year-over-year profit improvement, narrowing its EBIT loss as Gen-1 structural costs continue to come down toward our target of a 40% full-year profitability improvement in our Gen-1 portfolio. 3. Software and physical services are creating a high-margin recurring flywheel. Ford+ isn't just about selling a vehicle once; it's about building a lifelong relationship with the customer through digital and physical ecosystem services. In Q2, total paid customer subscriptions grew 50% year-over-year to 1.6 million, including over 900,000 Ford Pro Intelligence subscriptions. These are paid, active software subscriptions — not free bundled trials — proving that retail and commercial customers see genuine, day-to-day value in our software solutions. As this high-margin recurring layer scales, it creates a powerful margin flywheel across all three of our vehicle segments. 4. We are investing in high margin adjacent businesses such as Ford Energy. We are deploying capital into high-return adjacencies where Ford holds a clear competitive advantage. Following a milestone commercial agreement with EDF Power Solutions, Ford Energy is on track to achieve 20 gigawatt-hours of annual battery energy storage capacity by late 2027. This transforms our manufacturing footprints into active energy assets and opens up a lucrative, high-margin market in grid energy infrastructure. Looking Ahead Our results in the second quarter prove that when we execute with discipline, Ford wins. We possess a strong balance sheet, $22.3 billion in cash, and a clear capital allocation framework that allows us to fund high-return growth while returning value to shareholders — including a 15-cent regular dividend announced today. We have plenty of work ahead, but our strategy is clear, our team is aligned, and we are moving steadily toward our target of an 8% EBIT margin by 2029. Sherry House is Chief Financial Officer at Ford Motor Company.

title: Meet the Real-Life Superfan Starring in Spotify’s Fan Life Campaign
summary: How big of a fan are you of your favorite musical act? Have you recommended your favorite songs to friends and strangers alike? Have you forever memorialized their work on your body with a tattoo? Did your fandom, in some mystical twist of fate, lead to you meeting your significant other? Kye O’Hagan, a Geese...
body_text: How big of a fan are you of your favorite musical act? Have you recommended your favorite songs to friends and strangers alike? Have you forever memorialized their work on your body with a tattoo? Did your fandom, in some mystical twist of fate, lead to you meeting your significant other? Kye O’Hagan , a Geese superfan from Glasgow, can answer “yes” to all of those questions. And thanks to his love of the blazing-hot Brooklyn group, he’s one of the faces of Spotify’s latest Fan Life campaign, which begins rolling out around the world today with images that focus on the live concert experience. Fan Life celebrates real fans—the folks who bring years of memories, traditions, and participation to bear—by capturing their sacred and unique concert rituals, highlighting an experience that transforms music into community. NEXT Kye has been a Geese fan (call him a Goose) since 2021, when he heard a song from their first album on his Discover Weekly playlist. In the years since, he’s become a happy evangelist for the group. When he gets the aux cord at work, in a music shop, he’s often blasting tunes like “Taxes” and “Low Era.” He shares his recommendations with curious younger customers, and is working hard to convert older shopgoers, too. He’s also made more personal connections thanks to the band’s music. He has lyrics from the song “2122” tattooed on his wrists in a display of modern superfandom. “ A lot of my tattoos are arbitrary but the reason for this specific one…I just think it’s a truly great modern rock song,” he said. After bumping into a university classmate at a Geese show in 2023, the two became friends. After a while, that new friend’s roommate and Kye began dating. “It’s funny to think without Geese I wouldn’t be as happy as I am now,” Kye said. “The power of music!” https://storage.googleapis.com/pr-newsroom-wp/1/2026/07/FANLIFE_GEESE_16x9_WM-smaller.mp4 Spotify has always been the best place for fans, where they can get first access to tickets via Reserved , once-in-a-lifetime artist experiences , or exclusive artist content like Canvas videos and Countdown To episodes. Fan Life is all about recognizing and celebrating the power of fandom. That’s precisely why you’ll see Kye rocking out with fellow superfans—all of them in crocheted goose beanies—in our latest campaign. And you’ll see members of other global fandoms, too, including supporters of A$AP Rocky , Rosalía , Zara Larsson , and more. Caring about something is a powerful way of sharing your identity, as Kye well knows. “I loved that I became known as the Geese fan to all my friends,” he said. “It’s always fun to be associated with something, but it’s even better when it’s a band you love.”

title: All Out Fitness on Reinventing the Sports Industry with Unified Payment Processing
summary: From a pandemic home gear store to an one-stop-fitness-shop, All Out Fitness scaled across gyms, retail, and major sporting events by eliminating friction. Learn how they partner with PayMongo to run three distinct revenue streams seamlessly through one unified financial system.
body_text: Before gyms were shut down in 2020, MPG Powerhouse Fitness was already an established CrossFit gym. With physical training on hold and the entire country stuck at home, the team saw an opening: Filipinos who couldn't go to the gym still wanted to move, and they were going to need equipment to do it. That insight launched All Out Fitness, a training company built to supply the home gym market that the pandemic was rapidly creating. What started as a response to lockdowns has grown into something more deliberate: a fitness brand operating as one interconnected ecosystem that serves athletes, home gym builders, event-goers, and corporate fitness partners — all under one roof. Multiple Businesses, One Playbook All Out Fitness today runs across three distinct categories: gyms, equipment supplying, and sporting events. Each has its own team and point person, but the three are designed to feed each other. The gym side now operates two branches — the original CrossFit-focused facility, and a newer hybrid gym built around functional fitness and HYROX-style movements. Both serve the same community of athletes that All Out Fitness has cultivated since its early days. The equipment arm — the Shopify-powered online store at alloutfitnessph.com — sells the full range: barbells, plates, racks, conditioning gear, mats, recovery tools, accessories, and packages. The product line is specifically curated for CrossFit and hybrid training, making it a natural extension of the gym rather than a separate business. The mission, as the brand states it: to empower people to reach their full physical and mental potential through affordable, top-quality fitness equipment, welcoming spaces, and transformative programs — becoming the nation's most trusted name in gym equipment. The events vertical is where they get innovative. Equipment that isn’t sold through the store gets deployed at events. These events drive community engagement, which builds brand loyalty, which drives gym memberships and equipment sales. Nothing goes to waste. All Out Fitness at an outdoor sporting event Business Expansion The early days were lean. At the height of the pandemic, the entire operation ran on two employees who handled packaging, orders, and delivery simultaneously. When restrictions were lifted, the demand for fitness was immediate. Gyms reopened to members who were more motivated about health than they'd ever been. The home gym market that All Out Fitness had been building during lockdowns kept growing, as Filipinos who'd developed workout habits at home continued investing in their setups. That momentum opened doors to bigger opportunities. All Out Fitness has partnered with Bench Active, supplying equipment for their hybrid race series — the second leg of which has already run, with a third on the way. They're also supplying the Sip Plus Games, a multi-sport event coming in July. And since 2023, All Out Fitness has hosted its own flagship competition: the All Out Games, an annual event for the CrossFit community that has grown into one of the more significant gatherings in the local functional fitness calendar. The pattern is consistent: show up in the spaces where your community already is, then create more opportunities for them. PayMongo Across All Three Verticals All Out Fitness has integrated PayMongo since the online store launched — embedded into the website from the start, handling all incoming payments across the product catalog. The primary tool for in-person and event transactions is QR Ph, managed through multiple QR codes set up for different revenue streams. One for gym membership payments, equipment sales, and walk-in customers. Events get their own dedicated code, which means the standee travels to every Bench Active race, every All Out Game, and more — ready to accept payments on the spot without any setup friction. "Everyone's using e-wallets today," Finance representative Jessica notes. "And PayMongo is very useful on our website." The QR setup isn't just convenient — it's operationally necessary for a business running three distinct revenue streams tracked separately. Multiple QR codes routed to the same dashboard means finance can see what's coming in from memberships versus equipment sales versus events, without manually sorting through mixed records. Jessica specifically admires the PayMongo dashboard’s flexibility in customizable payout schedules. Previously locked to weekly payouts, All Out Fitness can now choose between weekly, twice-weekly, or monthly settlement — adjusting based on what the business needs at any given time. For a multi-vertical operation with different cash flow rhythms across gym, trading, and events, that control is a big deal. She also notes the customer support’s quick responses. "Fast to reply," Jessica says — which, for a finance manager running payments across three business lines, is the kind of reliability that builds long-term trust in a platform. A close-up of All Out Fitness' event setup, including their QR Ph standee Growths & Gains The growth plan is structured and deliberate: one new gym branch per year, and four events annually. Both targets reflect the same logic that's driven All Out Fitness since the beginning — expand into sporting communities. The events calendar in particular signals how far the brand has come from its pandemic-era origins. That position in the community is the brand's most durable asset, and the expansion plan is built around protecting and deepening it. Payments On-The-Go All Out Fitness represents a use case that PayMongo's QR Ph infrastructure is built for: a multi-location, multi-vertical business that needs flexible, portable payment acceptance without the overhead of separate systems for each part of the operation. Multiple QR codes, one dashboard, customizable payout schedules — together, these give All Out Fitness the visibility and control a finance manager needs to run clean books across gym memberships, equipment transactions, and live events. Most importantly, the payment experience for customers — whether they're renewing a gym membership, buying a barbell, or paying an event entry fee — is accessed through the same simple, hassle-free scan. For a brand whose entire value proposition is about going all out, having a payments setup that removes every unnecessary friction point is a core foundation for mastering their business operations. All Out Fitness is a PayMongo merchant based in the Philippines, operating across gym, fitness equipment retail, and sporting events. Visit them at alloutfitnessph.com.

title: Northwestern Mutual used Sprinklr AI to power its most successful social campaign ever
summary: Northwestern Mutual used Sprinklr AI to power its most successful social campaign ever
body_text: The Challenge In early September, Northwestern Mutual archived years of posts from its Instagram account. In a first-of-its-kind social campaign for the brand, the Milwaukee-based financial services company wiped its Instagram feed clean and launched the virtual Museum of Recent History, an ode to a cultural shift they’ve dubbed, “The Great Realization.” According to Senior Director of Social Marketing Whitney Magnuson, “It’s that moment where an individual’s priorities come into sharp focus, prompting them to re-architect their lives and pursue what matters most — with the support of a financial plan.” To support this seven-day campaign, Northwestern Mutual needed a technical solution that would: Help it to evaluate the content types and themes that would resonate with its audience Enable easy collaboration between teams to create, share, approve, and publish social assets. Increase efficiency in its community management workflow “This was a well-executed and wildly successful campaign for us, and it was fully supported by the Sprinklr platform. Our teams are energized and inspired, and we’re excited to see what else we can dream up in partnership with Sprinklr.” Whitney Magnuson Senior Director, Social Marketing Northwestern Mutual The Solution The financial services organization leveraged the Sprinklr platform to help power its “Museum of Recent History” social campaign from start to finish. Benchmarking from Sprinklr Insights enabled Northwestern Mutual’s teams to compare and evaluate which content types and themes were resonating with fans and followers in the financial services industry. Sprinklr AI gathered and analyzed relevant content that helped teams optimize their strategy for the campaign. “This helped us in the brainstorming phase and enabled us to come up with ideas that would hit home with our audience,” says Magnuson. Once they had devised their campaign and designed creative assets, they leveraged the Asset Manager from Sprinklr Social . The Asset Manager enabled the creative, social and compliance teams to easily coordinate content — ensuring each asset was brand compliant, optimized for the platform and approved for publication. “Because of the size of the video files, using the Asset Manager was a critical step for this campaign, especially for Instagram story assets,” says Magnuson. Northwestern Mutual also used the Sprinklr Rule Engine to assist with and automate much of the community management workload. “With more than 50,000 engagements coming in over just seven days, the team needed help to make sure they were hiding any comments that would affect the brand or the integrity of the museum,” explains Magnuson. “And Sprinklr’s automated tools allowed us to do just that.” Magnuson’s team configured rules that helped moderate conversations on posts, hiding or deleting comments from known spam accounts and ensuring no sensitive or inappropriate content was displayed. The Outcome Northwestern Mutual’s “Museum of Recent History” campaign set two social marketing records for the company: In just seven days, the campaign’s social posts received more than 57,000 engagements, a 10X increase from the same week one year ago. Within the campaign, a single post received 31,000 likes, making it the most liked Instagram post in the company’s history. While gaining additional followers was not one of the goals of the campaign, their optimized content also attracted an additional 300 followers. “This was a well-executed and wildly successful campaign for us, and it was fully supported by the Sprinklr platform,” says Magnuson. “Our teams are energized and inspired, and we’re excited to see what else we can dream up in partnership with Sprinklr.”

title: Alaska Airlines | Hawaiian Airlines Foundation awards $285K to first round of grantees
summary: Grants focus on uplifting the next generation and preserving heritage across the states of Alaska and Hawaiʻi.
body_text: The Alaska Trail Stewards (ATS) program provides volunteer-based trail construction and maintenance services to public land managers and others who have the responsibility to safely and sustainably maintain trails throughout Alaska. Its goals are to increase the number of skilled and safe volunteers doing trail work on public lands in Alaska, provide a wide variety of opportunities for citizen stewardship of public lands, decrease the backlog of trail maintenance on public lands, and expand youth engagement in caring for public lands. ATS volunteer events are held on public lands from Seward to Talkeetna, Alaska. The organization collaborates with land managers from Chugach National Forest, Chugach State Park, Hatcher Pass State Park, Denali State Park, the City of Whittier, the Municipality of Anchorage and the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to identify priority trail projects that volunteers can accomplish. Volunteers complete work such as trail brushing to clear alders and other brush encroaching on the trail, digging drainage ditches and constructing trail structures such as step-and-run boardwalk.

body_text: Base44 AI is an ai app builder that turns natural language prompts into working web apps - complete with frontend UI, backend logic, database, user authentication, and built in hosting. If you've been evaluating tools for rapid prototyping or lightweight internal tools, Base44 has likely appeared on your radar. This guide breaks down how the platform works, what it costs, where it fits, and where it falls short for production-grade use. Key Takeaways Base44 is an ai-powered no-code platform that generates fully functional apps from plain English descriptions in minutes. It was acquired by WIX in mid-2026 for around $80 million, positioning it squarely in the "vibe coding" wave - describe your app idea, get a working app back. Base44 utilizes generative AI to handle frontend, backend, and database development from a single prompt, with no coding required. It is designed for small and medium-sized businesses and startups looking for rapid prototyping and MVP development.
